newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina seen heading for another big cotton crop.
newsitem.headline: Argentina seen heading for another big cotton crop.

text.p: Argentine farmers are preparing another big cotton campaign, partly because the weather has not allowed them to diversify into wheat or sunflower seed, a top cotton exporter reported Wednesday.
"It is possible to predict a cotton area, weather permitting, from between 900,000 to one million hectares," said cotton exporter Almiroty y Compania in a report.
Farmers spent June, July and August preparing soil, and received long-awaited rains at the end of September. Rainfall was generally 30-40 mm in cotton zones, Almiroty said.
"This should allow early sowing of cotton, spreading sowing out over time and avoiding harvest bottlenecks," Almiroty said, but added that many farmers were troubled by a lack of credit.

Farmers planted a record one million hectares in 1995/96, with final production totaling around 425,000 tonnes of lint, Almiroty said. This was up from sown area of 700,000 hectares the previous season and from just 300,000 to 400,000 hectares in most recent years.
Most of Argentina's cotton is exported, with the troubled local textile industry taking about 100,000 tonnes of lint.
